arithmetic.crowding_prediction: n=120 on 120 cells, k=6.7 per cell -> income/k = 0.30; n=30 on 120 cells, k=1 -> income 2.0, a factor 6.7 higher
arithmetic.stock_prediction: a cell eaten every step only holds what regrew (0.2 per step by default), so the income is near 0.2-0.3 at both densities
arithmetic.discriminator: the ratio of income at n=30 to income at n=120: near 6.7 means crowding, near 1 means stock

silent.evidence: one organism alone on 120 cells takes 0.30519045226130653 per step, so no crowding is needed for the income to be low

specific.evidence: income n=30 / n=120 = 1.00, below the midpoint 2.6 between crowding (6.7) and stock (1.0)

verdict.reason: income n=30/n=120 = 1.00 (crowding predicts 6.7, stock predicts 1.0); a lone organism takes 0.30519045226130653 per step, so the limit is the cell stock, not the number of organisms

limitations: income is recovered from the energy drop, so it assumes the step cost is 0.2 + move_cost*moved; EXP-39 supports that
the trace does not report the cell stock, so "stock" is inferred from the absence of crowding, not read directly
one seed and one regrow (the default 0.2); a higher regrow would separate the two predictions more sharply and was not tried
